provenance.paper: Reiter, R. (1991). The frame problem in the situation calculus: a simple solution (sometimes) and a completeness result for goal regression.
provenance.citation: Reiter, R. (1991). In V. Lifschitz (Ed.), Artificial Intelligence and Mathematical Theory of Computation: Papers in Honor of John McCarthy (pp. 359-380). Academic Press.
provenance.locus: Sections 2-3: successor-state axioms F(do(a,s)) ≡ γ+_F(a,s) ∨ (F(s) ∧ ¬γ-_F(a,s)); blocks-world pickup/putdown running example.
provenance.notes: Blocks-world pickup/putdown instance of Reiter's successor-state axiomatization. The frame problem's solution is exhibited by fluents (on_b_table, color_b_red) untouched by the action sequence persisting purely by inertia — no frame axioms enumerated per fluent/action pair.

input.intent: progress blocks world through pickup(a); putdown(a, table)

expected.notes: on_b_table and color_b_red are never mentioned by any executed action's add/del list, so they persist by Reiter inertia and must each be named in a frame-persist trace step.
